items.title: A nontrivial universal homeomorphism of spectra yields either square and cube relations or a prime and a p-th power relation
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that a nontrivial ring extension whose spectrum map is a universal homeomorphism contains either an element outside the base with square and cube in the base, or an element outside the base with a prime multiple and a p-th power in the base (statement lines 11656-11663). The counted proof, 45 lines, is written out in full by the author even though it parallels an earlier argument: it reduces to an integral extension generated by one element and then finite, localizes at a minimal prime of the support of the quotient, identifies the unique prime of the extension over the maximal ideal of the base through the annihilator of the quotient, and then splits into the two alternatives, the second of which uses pure inseparability of the residue field extension in prime characteristic to build the required element (proof lines 11665-11709). It is H2 under the lane rule: the proof contains checkable reductions and a construction of the witnessed element in each alternative, and the opening sentence in which the author says the argument is almost the same as an earlier one is immediately followed by the full argument, so nothing is deferred.
